subject: Licensing matrix + seat-to-capacity reconciliation for Clearline
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Yu <sarah.yu@clearline.ai>, procurement@clearline.ai
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Licensing matrix + seat-to-capacity reconciliation for Clearline

Hi Sarah / procurement team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we finalize pricing and the contract term, we need to reconcile two practical points so the licensing in the SOW matches how you actually plan to consume capacity:

1) Seat pooling vs dedicated seats — are you intending to share a pool of seats across teams (preferred for bursty workloads) or lock dedicated seats per team?
2) Peak concurrency vs average usage — we saw a range in the telemetry; we want to align on how many concurrent inference slots to reserve vs rely on burst capacity.

Attached is a proposed licensing matrix (clearline_license_matrix.xlsx) with two options:
- Option A: Seat-based with per-seat add-ons for high-throughput pipelines
- Option B: Throughput buckets (preferred if you want predictable per-token unit economics) + seat access for admin users

Can you confirm which model maps to your procurement needs? If you prefer, we can run a quick call to walk the matrix. My ask: reply with which option you prefer and any constraints from procurement (billing cadence, PO requirements).

I'll keep Kimberly and Ben in the loop — Kimberly will scope any concession if we need to move off list pricing.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: clearline_license_matrix.xlsx, redwood_proposal_v3.pdf

From: Sarah Yu <sarah.yu@clearline.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Licensing matrix + seat-to-capacity reconciliation for Clearline

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the file. A few clarifying points from our side:

- We plan to centralize inference calls through a shared infra team (so seat pooling is preferred), but product teams will expect predictable monthly spend per project.
- Our procurement team needs to understand overage rates if usage spikes exceed reserved throughput for a month. We also need the cancellation window for any reserved capacity.

A couple quick asks: can you show a pricing example for a 12-month commit with a 20% variance buffer on monthly usage? Also, what discounts apply at the $250k and $500k ARR thresholds?

Procurement can also accept DocuSign for signatures. I cc'd procurement@clearline.ai so they can flag any PO requirements.

Appreciate it — available for a 30-minute call Wed afternoon if that helps.

Best,
Sarah Yu
Head of Finance | Clearline AI

Note: we didn't receive the detailed overage language in the PDF — can you surface that?

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Yu <sarah.yu@clearline.ai>, procurement@clearline.ai
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Licensing matrix + seat-to-capacity reconciliation for Clearline

Sarah — thanks for the quick reply. Answers inline and next steps below.

- Seat pooling: Option B (throughput buckets + admin seats) maps best to centralized infra while giving product teams predictable monthly spend.
- Overage rates: we propose a two-tier overage model (buffers applied hourly then billed monthly):
  • 0–20% overage: billed at 1.25x unit price (soft buffer)
  • >20%: billed at 1.6x unit price (excess)
  • Cancellation: 60-day notice for reserved capacity reductions; immediate prorate for increases.

Pricing examples (excerpt from attached redwood_proposal_v3.pdf):
- 12-month commit, baseline 200k token units/month, 20% buffer: effective blended rate = $0.00095/token-equivalent (example)
- Discount bands: $250k ARR -> 8% discount; $500k ARR -> 15% discount (applied to reserved capacity portion only).

Attached the clarified matrix (I updated the overage rows and added sample math). Two options for signing:
- Option 1: Standard term (12 month, 60-day reduction) + listed discounts
- Option 2: 12-month commit + 6-month true-up window + extra 5% concession on reserved capacity if you commit to invoice in advance (annual prepay)

If procurement is comfortable, we can push Option 2 to legal and I can have a draft DocuSign (with concession reflected) back to you today. If you'd rather, we can take 30 minutes Wed 4pm PT to walk through.

Next asks: Sarah/procurement — which Option do you lean toward? If Option 2, procurement confirms PO/advance-invoice acceptance and I will send DocuSign.

Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v3.pdf (updated), clearline_license_matrix.xlsx (updated)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sarah Yu <sarah.yu@clearline.ai>, procurement@clearline.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Licensing matrix + seat-to-capacity reconciliation for Clearline

Looping in quickly — Jordan, if Clearline wants Option 2 and agrees to annual prepay, we can offer an additional one-time implementation credit of $12,500 (applied as invoice credit) and a stepped cadence for excess bursting: first 2 months of overage waived for initial ramp in year 1.

Ben — please note for forecasting this concession.

Sarah — happy to confirm concessions in the DocuSign draft. We typically need a written PO referencing the DocuSign envelope id for accounting to accept the prepay.

Kimberly Park
Director, Mid-Market Sales | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Attachment: internal_note_concessions.md (internal)

From: Sarah Yu <sarah.yu@clearline.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearline.ai, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Licensing matrix + seat-to-capacity reconciliation for Clearline

Kimberly / Jordan — thank you. Procurement reviewed Option 2 and is comfortable with annual prepay and the concession structure. They asked for two small changes before sign:

1) Add explicit language that the implementation credit applies within 90 days of the contract start date.
2) Add a clause that the first true-up window can be shifted to month 9 if we provide forecasted usage by month 6.

If you can incorporate those two bullets into the DocuSign and send the updated envelope, procurement will route the PO immediately. We prefer DocuSign + PO reference (we will send PO to procurement@redwood.ai once envelope id is shown).

If you want me on a quick call to confirm language, I can make 4pm PT on Monday. Otherwise please send the updated DocuSign.

Best,
Sarah Yu
Head of Finance | Clearline AI

Requested attachments: updated DocuSign (include envelope id), final redwood_proposal_v3.pdf (with concession lines)
